A1.justification: Both PDFs are fully readable versions of the same UI2C study, with matching sections, six figures, three tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains the appendix or supplementary material mentioned in the text; the comparison covers all supplied pages.

before.justification: v5 reports original video-compression experiments, including benchmark results, encoding/decoding speeds, intra-coding comparisons, and component ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and the experimental figures.

M1.justification: The unified intra/inter model, simultaneous two-frame compression, two-frame quantization, and hybrid-reference training remain unchanged. Figure 3's caption correction matches components already present in the original diagram.

E1.justification: Both versions use Vimeo-90k and longer Vimeo sequences for training, and HEVC Classes B–E, UVG, and MCL-JCV for evaluation. The first-two-frame and scene-change scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VTM-17.0, DCVC-DC, DCVC-FM, and DCVC-RT. Figure 5 retains the DCVC-RT-I-intra and DCVC-RT-P-intra comparisons. The bibliography replacement does not change evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The YUV420 low-delay evaluation, intra-period of −1, entropy-based bitrate estimation, QP settings, and testing procedures are unchanged. Table 2 clarifies per-frame reporting without revising the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same ablations of unified coding, two-frame compression, hybrid references, and refresh. The intra-coding comparison in Figure 5 and sequence-level analyses in Figures 1 and 6 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. Existing averaging across datasets and QPs is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and plotted results are unchanged. Both report an average BD-rate of −12.1% relative to DCVC-RT and encoding/decoding speeds of 65.1/46.1 fps for UI2C.

T1.justification: The mathematical relationships and assumptions used to describe the method are unchanged. No formal definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified coding, reduced error propagation without manual refresh, two-frame compression, and a 12.1% average BD-rate reduction with real-time operation.

C2.justification: The explanations of error propagation and coding efficiency remain unchanged. Both retain qualifications concerning shorter sequences, one-frame latency, edge-device speed, and high-bitrate performance.

D1.justification: Hardware specifications, training loss, QP settings, data-source links, and code-access information are unchanged. Table 2 makes per-frame averaging explicit in its footnote, consistent with the explanation already present in Section 4.3; it introduces no new implementation setting.

R1.justification: v6 removes the HyTIP citation, reference [6] in v5, and adds Tang et al.'s Neural video compression with reference hierarchy, reference [38] in v6, to the introductory survey. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 adds Tencent Shannon Lab affiliations, a funding/GPU-cluster acknowledgment, and a corresponding-author note. Caption and table-footnote wording receive small corrections; the section order and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3's caption changes the duplicated pair (FE1, FE1) to (FE1, FE2). Table 2 adds shared footnote markers explaining that latent channels and decoding steps are per-frame averages. Body text reflows slightly, while figure graphics, table structures, and numerical entries remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves clarity by correcting Figure 3's feature-extractor labels and making Table 2's per-frame accounting explicit at the point of use. These changes reduce ambiguity, while the method, experimental evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
